messages:
maria: quick check — EU customer (tier-enterprise bank) is asking for cryptographic proof that their BYOK master key never left their HSM during onboarding. they specifically want: signed wrap/unwrap receipts, chain-of-custody stamp for the import session, and an API-level acknowledgment we can hand to compliance. any minimal audit artifacts we can safely give without leaking key material? :thinking:
kevin: you can't provide raw key material obviously. we can provide signed receipts from our HSM-proxy showing the wrap operation occurred and the HSM attestation blob (cert chain) that proves the import session parameters. those blobs are non-secret. also include timestamped operation IDs and operator IDs (RBAC) — that helps legal.
sophie: +1. also record the exact firmware/slot ID and nonce used in the import. customers often want a verifiable nonce in the attestation so it can't be replayed. we should avoid including any full key fingerprints that could be used to correlate across customers.
maria: good. legal flagged they might request this under subpoena later — do we have an internal SLA for handing the attestations and do we redact operator hostnames? @legal-team any prescriptions?
legal-team: from a compliance perspective, preferred artifacts are: (1) HSM attestation certs (chain), (2) signed operation log entry (not containing key material), (3) operator and timestamp records, (4) export of relevant audit logs with tamper-evidence checksums. redact personal hostnames unless needed for incident triage. also document the chain-of-custody steps in the handoff packet.
ben: for the signed operation log entry, we can generate a detached signature over a compact JSON receipt. example: ```json
{"event":"import","key_id":"cust-987","actor":"hsm-proxy-01","attestation_cert":"MIIB...","timestamp":"2026-03-15T14:22:01Z"}
```
the signature is created by our escrow-signing key. that keeps the receipt verifiable but doesn't expose secrets.
oncall-bot: deploy scheduled: hsm-proxy: v2.7.3 will rollout at 15:45 UTC (canary 1/10). reaction :rocket:
kevin: small operational note — do not log full attestation blobs to high-retention analytics. keep them in sealed audit store (WORM) with strict RBAC. we should add a retention policy for evidence exports (e.g., 7 years for regulated customers).
sophie: also add a flag in the API to emit a "receipt_id" after import that the customer can fetch. receipt fetch returns only signed metadata and certificate chain, not keys. that satisfies many auditors.
maria: sounds like an action list: 1) prod runbook update describing evidence packet (attestation certs, receipt JSON + signature, operator audit lines); 2) RBAC check to limit who can export attestation blobs; 3) add API receipt_id endpoint and docs; 4) retention/expiry policy for exported packets. anyone want to pick steps?
ben: i'll draft the receipt JSON schema and a sample signature flow.
kevin: i'll update RBAC config and add audit-store retention tags.
sophie: i'll own the API changes and sample client snippet.
legal-team: i'll draft the legal wording for customer handoff and subpoena checklist. include redaction guidance.
maria: thanks everyone. last Q: for incident response, if a customer requests live evidence during an ongoing investigation, do we have a preferred triage flow? i'd rather avoid ad-hoc exports.
ben: prefer tabletop first. if urgent, use escalation path: SRE -> Security oncall -> Legal signoff, then we do a WORM export with signed receipt and watermark the export with the incident ID. log that export as an auditable operation.
kevin: ensure operator JIT access is logged and ephemeral. no manual SFTP of blobs. use pre-signed, time-limited retrieval links recorded in the audit store.
maria: perfect. i'll open a small RFC and link to this thread. tagging the action owners. :white_check_mark:
